about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Manhattan Tomato Chowder with Clams
recipes.summary: A tomato-based chowder with potato, celery and tender clams, lighter than the creamy kind.
steps: Cook the bacon in the oil in a large pot for 4 minutes until it renders and crisps.
Add the onion, celery, carrot and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the potatoes, tomatoes, stock and thyme, then simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the clams and heat through for 3 minutes. Scatter with parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through, heat the clams until steaming hot and opaque at 75°C, and keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Serve with crackers.

recipes.title: Creamy White Fish Chowder with Thyme
recipes.summary: A chunky chowder of white fish, potato and sweetcorn in a gently thickened milk base.

items: 500 g firm white fish fillets, cubed

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion and celery for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock, milk, potatoes and thyme.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the corn and fish and poach gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in the cream and parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque throughout and the chowder steaming at 75°C, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Do not boil hard once the fish is in or it will break up.

recipes.title: Prawn Bisque
recipes.summary: A silky, deeply flavoured bisque made from prawn shells, tomato paste and a splash of cream.
steps: Peel the prawns and keep the shells. Refrigerate the prawn meat.
Fry the shells in the butter for 5 minutes until bright orange and fragrant.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika.
Add the rice and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Blend well and strain through a sieve, pressing out all the liquid.
Return to the pot, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and curled. Stir in the cream and lemon juice.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque and firm, and bring the bisque to 75°C before serving. Keep leftovers refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
The rice thickens the soup so no flour is needed.

recipes.title: Crab and Sweetcorn Bisque
recipes.summary: A smooth corn bisque finished with sweet crab meat and a swirl of cream.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the corn, stock and paprika and simmer for 12 minutes until the corn is tender.
Blend with the milk until very smooth, then return to the pot.
Stir in the cream and crab and warm gently for 3 minutes until steaming. Add the lemon juice.
Ladle into bowls and serve with chives on top.
notes: Food safety: use fresh, refrigerated crab meat, heat until the crab is opaque and the bisque a steaming 75°C. Eat leftovers within 2 days.
Strain for a restaurant style finish.

recipes.title: Mushroom Bisque
recipes.summary: An earthy, velvety soup of browned mushrooms, thyme and cream, with no flour needed.
steps: Cook the mushrooms in the butter in a large pot over high heat for 8 minutes until deeply golden.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the potato, stock and soy sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and reheat until steaming. Scatter with parsley.
notes: Reserve a few fried mushroom slices to garnish.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Roasted Butternut Bisque
recipes.summary: Roasted pumpkin blended with apple and a touch of cream for a sweet, silky soup.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and toss the pumpkin, apple and onion with the oil and cumin on a tray.
Roast for 35 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges.
Blend with the stock until smooth and warm in a pot until steaming.
Stir in the cream and nutmeg, then scatter with pepitas.
notes: Skip the cream and use coconut milk for a dairy free version.
Freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Salmon and Leek Chowder
recipes.summary: Fresh salmon, sweet leek and potato in a creamy, dill-scented chowder.

items: 400 g salmon fillet, skinned and cubed

steps: Melt the butter and cook the leeks for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, stock and milk and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Crush a few potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the salmon and poach gently for 4 minutes until opaque and just cooked through.
Stir in the cream, dill, lemon juice and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque throughout and the chowder steaming at 75°C. Eat leftovers within 2 days.
Do not boil once the salmon is in.

recipes.title: Potato and Bacon Chowder
recipes.summary: A thick, hearty potato soup loaded with smoky bacon, chives and a little cheddar.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot for 6 minutes until crisp, then lift half out for garnish.
Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour.
Add the stock, milk and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes roughly, stir in the cheddar and pepper until melted.
Serve with the crisp bacon and chives.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through and bring the chowder to a steaming 75°C. Keep leftovers refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
Use a little less cheddar for a lighter bowl.

recipes.title: Roasted Tomato and Basil Bisque
recipes.summary: Slow roasted tomatoes and garlic blended into a rich, creamy soup with fresh basil.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the oil for 35 minutes until collapsed and caramelised.
Squeeze the garlic from the skins and tip everything into a pot with the stock and sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then blend with the basil until smooth.
Stir in the cream and pepper and reheat until steaming.
notes: Serve with a grilled cheese sandwich.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or freezes for 3 months.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Cold Vermicelli Bowl with Lemongrass Beef
recipes.summary: Cool rice vermicelli with fresh herbs, pickled carrot and sizzling lemongrass beef.
steps: Mix the beef with the lemongrass, garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce and half the sugar.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the lime juice, remaining fish sauce, sugar and water into a dressing.
Sear the beef in the oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Divide the noodles, vegetables, herbs and beef between bowls and finish with peanuts and dressing.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef until browned with no pink inside, and cook the beef to at least 71°C, and keep any raw marinated meat refrigerated until cooking.
Use grilled tofu for a vegetarian bowl.

recipes.title: Korean Bibim Guksu Spicy Cold Noodles
recipes.summary: Chewy wheat noodles tossed in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce with crunchy vegetables and egg.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until the yolks are set, then cool in iced water and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender, then rinse well under cold water.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and garlic into a sauce.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then top with cucumber, kimchi, egg and sesame seeds.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add more gochujang for extra heat.

recipes.title: Thai Glass Noodle Salad with Prawns
recipes.summary: Slippery glass noodles with prawns, lime, chilli and fresh herbs in a bright Thai dressing.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for 5 minutes until soft and translucent, then drain and cut.
Poach the prawns in simmering water for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque, then drain.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the noodles, prawns, carrot, onion and herbs with the dressing and top with peanuts.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink, firm and opaque throughout, and keep the salad chilled until serving.
Serve straight away so the noodles stay slippery.

recipes.title: Chilled Buckwheat Noodles with Ginger Soy Edamame
recipes.summary: Nutty buckwheat noodles with edamame, cucumber and a sharp ginger soy dressing.
steps: Cook the soba in boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes.
Drain and rinse under cold water until the noodles are cold.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, sesame oil and honey together.
Toss with the noodles, cucumber and spring onions, then scatter with sesame seeds.
notes: Rinsing removes the surface starch so the noodles do not clump.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Somen Noodle Salad with Tomato and Shiso
recipes.summary: Fine chilled somen with juicy tomato, cucumber and a light citrus soy dressing.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes until tender, then rinse in iced water and drain well.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, lemon juice and sesame oil.
Toss the noodles with the tomato, cucumber and mint, then pour over the dressing and top with sesame seeds.
notes: Mint stands in for shiso if you cannot find it.
Serve very cold on a hot day.

recipes.title: Cold Dan Dan Noodle Salad
recipes.summary: Sesame and chilli noodles dressed in a nutty Sichuan style sauce with cucumber and peanuts.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil, sugar, garlic and warm water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then top with cucumber, spring onions and peanuts.
notes: Add more chilli oil for heat.
Sauce can be made 3 days ahead.

recipes.title: Cold Sesame Tofu Noodle Bowl
recipes.summary: Cold noodles with silken tofu, cucumber and a soy sesame dressing for a no-cook lunch.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes until tender, then rinse cold and drain.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar and sugar together.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, cucumber and carrot.
Top with the tofu, spring onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Handle the silken tofu gently so it stays in cubes.
Use extra firm tofu if you prefer more bite.

recipes.title: Rice Noodle Bowl with Peanut Lime Tofu
recipes.summary: Cool rice noodles, crunchy raw vegetables and crisp tofu in a peanut lime sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse cold and drain.
Pan-fry the tofu in the oil for 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, sugar and water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and vegetables, then top with tofu, coriander and peanuts.
notes: Thin the sauce with extra water if it is too thick.
Keeps well for a packed lunch.

recipes.title: Apple Oat Pancakes for Kids
recipes.summary: Soft, naturally sweet pancakes made from apple and oats with no added sugar.
steps: Blend the apples, oats, eggs, milk, baking powder and cinnamon until smooth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Stack on plates and serve with a spoonful of yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is set and no longer wet, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Freeze cooked pancakes and reheat in the toaster.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter and Apple Toast Fingers
recipes.summary: Wholemeal toast spread with smooth peanut butter and thin apple slices, cut into fingers for small hands.
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread with the peanut butter and top with the apple slices.
Dust with cinnamon and cut into fingers.
notes: Use a nut-free spread such as sunflower seed butter for school and childcare settings.
Cut into small pieces for toddlers.

recipes.title: Rainbow Fruit and Yoghurt Pots
recipes.summary: Layers of mango, berries and orange over creamy yoghurt, no sweetener needed.
steps: Spoon a layer of yoghurt into four small cups or jars.
Add layers of mango, berries and orange.
Repeat the layers until the cups are full and top with the toasted oats just before serving.
notes: Keep the toasted oats separate until serving so it stays crisp.
Make the pots the night before for a quick breakfast.

recipes.title: Cheesy Scrambled Egg Fingers
recipes.summary: Soft scrambled egg with a little grated cheddar, spooned over toast fingers.
steps: Whisk the eggs and milk together.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes until set but still soft.
Fold through the cheddar until it melts.
Toast the bread until golden, cut into fingers and top with the egg.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and no longer runny, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Leave out salt for babies and toddlers.

recipes.title: Apple Oat Breakfast Muffins
recipes.summary: Wholegrain muffins sweetened only with apple and a little honey, ideal for school mornings.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 12 hole muffin tin.
Mix the oats, flour and cinnamon, then stir in the apples.
Whisk the eggs, milk, honey and oil, then fold into the dry mix until just combined.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean so the egg is fully cooked.
Freeze for up to 3 months.
